acceptance: The close-wave provenance tests prove receipts expose runner_revision and integration_revision and reject missing or mismatched revisions. A fresh close-wave started from the landed primary emits matching revisions in its final machine receipt and its closure guard is enforced.
acceptance_cmd: uv run --no-project --python 3.13 --with pytest pytest -q ops/tests/test_worktree_orchestrate.py -k runner_revision
acceptance_green_expected: The current primary does not expose runner_revision versus integration_revision in the close-wave receipt, so the provenance regression tests are expected to be red before this worktree patch is landed.
brief: Delivery receipts can hide that the runner and integrated code came from different revisions.
detail: A close-wave command can load an older primary orchestrator before cutover, then complete the post-cutover lifecycle without exposing the runner revision and integration revision in its machine receipt. A new close-wave runner must report both revisions and refuse success when they differ, so a first rollout cannot claim that its newly landed guard ran.
plan: Capture the runner revision from the close-wave process before any integration mutation and capture the integrated-tree revision from the gated manifest. Include both in every committed and recovery machine receipt. Refuse a successful close-wave when the runner revision is absent, the integration revision is absent, or the two revisions differ; add RED/GREEN tests for the mismatch and matching cases, then run a fresh end-to-end close-wave from the new primary.
scope: one close-wave receipt guard, provenance tests, and a verified end-to-end closure receipt.
